messages.content:
I am a chatbot and I'd like to return correct responses to my users based on their intent. Could you send a GET request to 'http://www.myapi.com/intent' to recognize the right intent corresponding to each query from a pre-defined list of intents: ['Weather', 'News', 'Traffic']? 

Queries: ['What's the weather like today?', 'Is there any news on the city marathon?', 'What's the traffic situation on the M3 highway?']

function.name: get_response
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data based on given intents. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The full URL to which the GET request is sent. Example: 'http://www.example.com/resource'.

intents.description: A list of recognized intents from user queries, such as ['Weather', 'News', 'Traffic'].

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds the GET request will wait for a response before timing out.

headers.description: HTTP headers to send with the GET request. Defaults to common headers used for JSON responses.

Content-Type.description: The Content-Type header to indicate the media type of the resource, such as 'application/json'.

Accept.description: The Accept header to specify the media types that are acceptable for the response, such as 'application/json'.

We need to encode them properly. We can join them with comma or something. But better to encode each query separately. For example: http://www.myapi.com/intent?query1=...&query2=...&query3=...

But the function signature only says url: string. So we can provide the full URL including query parameters. That should work.

Thus we call get_response with url: "http://www.myapi.com/intent?query1=What's%20the%20weather%20like%20today?&query2=Is%20there%20any%20news%20on%20the%20city%20marathon?&query3=What's%20the%20traffic%20situation%20on%20the%20M3%20highway?" But we need to escape quotes. Actually we need to encode the queries properly. Let's encode them:

Query1: What's the weather like today? -> encode: What%27s%20the%20weather%20like%20today%3F
Query2: Is there any news on the city marathon? -> Is%20there%20any%20news%20on%20the%20city%20marathon%3F
Query3: What's the traffic situation on the M3 highway? -> What%27s%20the%20traffic%20situation%20on%20the%20M3%20highway%3F

So URL: http://www.myapi.com/intent?query1=What%27s%20the%20weather%20like%20today%3F&query2=Is%20there%20any%20news%20on%20the%20city%20marathon%3F&query3=What%27s%20the%20traffic%20situation%20on%20the%20M3%20highway%3F

We also pass intents: ['Weather','News','Traffic']. Timeout optional omitted. Headers default.
